out.other_title: Two-turn debate with counter-arguments does not help humans answer hard QuALITY questions
out.rationale: Parrish et al.'s two-turn study (one argument plus one counter-argument) reports no accuracy gain, while Michael et al. report a positive debate result on the same dataset. The authors attribute the difference to their unbounded length, interaction and hidden-passage setup, and say absolute accuracies are not comparable, so the challenge is scoped to protocol.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: Whether multi-turn debate improves human judge accuracy on hard QuALITY questions; the contrast depends on debate length, judge interaction and expertise gap

text: The authors note that in Parrish et al.'s one- and two-turn debate experiments on QuALITY, debate did not significantly improve judge accuracy, and they point to differences from their own setting. The first is that their debates are unbounded in length rather than limited to a single refutation, which the authors suggest may produce more useful and informative arguments.
title: Michael et al. find debate helps QuALITY judges, unlike Parrish et al.'s two-turn null result
